O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Na lista do TSE, os candidatos são classificados em duas situações principais: concorrendo ou inapto.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

Esta reportagem foi produzida de modo automático com dados fornecidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ( clique aqui para saber mais) e pode ser atualizada em caso de mudança na lista de candidatos a deputado distrital no Distrito Federal. Caso você perceba algum erro, por favor nos informe por meio do formulário .

articles.body:
Mato Grosso do Sul (MS) tem 252 candidatos disputando 24 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Na lista do TSE, os candidatos são classificados em duas situações principais: concorrendo ou inapto.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

Esta reportagem foi produzida de modo automático com dados fornecidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ( clique aqui para saber mais) e pode ser atualizada em caso de mudança na lista de candidatos a deputado estadual em Mato Grosso do Sul. Caso você perceba algum erro, por favor nos informe por meio do formulário .

articles.summary: ES tem 410 candidatos na disputa por 30 vagas; votação será em 4 de outubro.
articles.body:
O Espírito Santo (ES) tem 410 candidatos disputando 30 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Na lista do TSE, os candidatos são classificados em duas situações principais: concorrendo ou inapto.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

Esta reportagem foi produzida de modo automático com dados fornecidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ( clique aqui para saber mais) e pode ser atualizada em caso de mudança na lista de candidatos a deputado estadual no Espírito Santo. Caso você perceba algum erro, por favor nos informe por meio do formulário .

articles.body:
A Paraíba (PB) tem 211 candidatos disputando 36 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

O Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar neste ano, segundo dados do TSE. Os votos serão para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual (ou distrital, apenas no caso do Distrito Federal). Todos os cargos têm mandato de quatro anos, exceto o de senador, cujo mandato é de oito anos.

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

Cassado com recurso, indeferido com recurso ou pedido não conhecido com recurso;

Em algumas listas, o mesmo candidato aparece mais de uma vez. O TSE informa que manterá os nomes duplicados, mas apontará apenas uma das opções como apta ("concorrendo") até o dia da eleição.

Esta reportagem foi produzida de modo automático com dados fornecidos pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ( clique aqui para saber mais) e pode ser atualizada em caso de mudança na lista de candidatos a deputado estadual na Paraíba. articles.body:
A Bahia (BA) tem 636 candidatos disputando 63 vagas na Assembleia Legislativa nas Eleições 2026, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A votação será realizada em 4 de outubro, e as vagas são distribuídas entre partidos e federações pelo sistema proporcional, para mandatos de quatro anos.

A lista abaixo traz os nomes e os números de urna dos candidatos, enviados pelos partidos ao TSE, e também a situação de cada um: se estão concorrendo ou inaptos para concorrer, conforme decisão da Justiça Eleitoral.

articles.title: Capivara flagrada com arco na cintura no Taquaral é capturada | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação se deu após denúncia de uma pessoa que passou pelo local e percebeu que o objeto estaria preso ao animal de forma "bastante apertada".
articles.summary: Ação se deu após denúncia de uma pessoa que passou pelo local e percebeu que o objeto estaria preso ao animal de forma "bastante apertada".
articles.body:
Capivara com arco na cintura é flagrada na Lagoa do Taquaral, em Campinas — Foto: Imagens Cedidas

Uma capivara flagrada com um arco preso à cintura na Lagoa do Taquaral, em Campinas (SP), foi capturada e atendida por um médico veterinário nesta terça-feira (1º). A informação foi confirmada pela Prefeitura.

A Secretaria do Clima, Meio Ambiente e Sustentabilidade (Seclimas) recebeu uma denúncia de uma pessoa que passou pelo local nesta segunda-feira (31). Segundo a denunciante, o objeto estaria preso ao animal de forma "bastante apertada".

A Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística do Estado de São Paulo (Semil) foi acionada para localizar e resgatar o animal. Após a captura, a capivara foi atendida por um médico veterinário.

Em maio deste ano, uma capivara em situações semelhantes mobilizou as equipes . Porém, na situação, o animal conseguiu pular na água e fugir dos agentes após diversas tentativas de captura.

De acordo com a Seclimas, não é possível afirmar se a capivara capturada neste caso é a mesma que conseguiu fugir anteriormente.

articles.title: JK não fez previsão sobre 'homem mau' assumindo Presidência do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Publicação falsa adulterou com inteligência artificial trecho de entrevista do ex-presidente Juscelino Kubitscheck sobre a construção de Brasília.
articles.summary: Publicação falsa adulterou com inteligência artificial trecho de entrevista do ex-presidente sobre a construção de Brasília.
articles.body:
É #FAKE vídeo de Juscelino Kubitschek prevendo 'homem mau' na Presidência do Brasil no século XXI; cena foi manipulada com IA — Foto: Reprodução

Circula nas redes sociais um vídeo que supostamente mostra uma entrevista do ex-presidente Juscelino Kubitscheck, que governou o país entre 1956 e 1961, dizendo que um "homem mau" se tornaria presidente do Brasil no século XXI. É #FAKE .

Publicado no TikTok em 16 de agosto, o vídeo exibe esta caixa de texto acima das imagens: "1974. A entrevista de Juscelino que nunca foi ao ar".

O vídeo em preto e branco mostra o ex-presidente Juscelino Kubitscheck sentado em uma cadeira enquanto fala sobre uma suposta previsão sobre o futuro político do Brasil — mas a gravação foi manipulada com inteligência artificial (leia mais abaixo) .

JK diz, dirigindo-se à câmera: "Certa vez eu consultei uma velha senhora que era de origem cigana e ela fez para mim uma previsão do futuro político do Brasil. Ela me disse que, por volta do ano 2000 e alguma coisa, iria surgir no nosso país um homem muito mau, um homem sem apreço à democracia [...] Ela me disse que este homem se tornará um grande político e que ficará conhecido em todo o país. " .

Ao longo do conteúdo, são exibidas diversas imagens do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL), sugerindo que ele seria o homem da "profecia".

No final da declaração, Juscelino diz que a pessoa se tornaria presidente do país e seria responsável pela morte de mais de 700 mil pessoas. "Eu fiquei muito assustado e não consegui dormir naquela noite. Passei a rezar e pedir a Deus que as previsões dessa velha cigana estejam erradas" .

O conteúdo manipulou um vídeo original de Juscelino Kubitscheck, no qual ele fala sobre a trajetória e os desafios da construção de Brasília, projeto implementado durante seu mandato como presidente . O Fato ou Fake transcreveu o vídeo e não encontrou qualquer menção relacionada à suposta previsão .

Originalmente, ele diz: "Eu vou contar só um episódio para dar o sentido da grandeza das dificuldades. Nós tínhamos que levar para lá um gerador de energia elétrica, um transformador que pesava 70 toneladas. Mas não havia uma estrada, uma carreta para sair de São Paulo e ir até Brasília. Era uma grande ventura tão grave, que eu chamei e pedi o batalhão de engenharia da cidade de Itajubá, batalhão de engenharia do exército para tomar a si o encargo, como se fosse uma operação de guerra [...]" .

O Fato ou Fake submeteu o conteúdo a três ferramentas de detecção de IA em vídeos e áudios, e todas acusaram o uso desse recurso. Veja os resultado das análises (e os infográficos ao final da reportagem):

HiveModeration - 66,2% de probabilidade de o áudio ter sido manipulado com IA e 79,4% de ser deepfake.

Hiya/Invid - 89% de chances de o áudio ter sido gerado por IA. "Hiya.com considera este fragmento de áudio como muito provavelmente gerada por IA".

Detector Mever/Invid - 98% de probabilidade de o conteúdo ter sido gerado por IA. "Detector Mever de vídeo deepfake. Probabilidade 98%. Provas muito sólidas". Esse método detecta rostos manipulados por deepfake.

➡️ Deepfake é uma técnica que permite alterar um vídeo ou foto com ajuda de inteligência artificial. Com ele, por exemplo, o rosto da pessoa que está em cena pode ser trocado pelo de outra e as próprias falas podem ser modificadas.

Para descobrir a origem do material, o Fato ou Fake usou a ferramenta InVID e fragmentou o vídeo em frames (imagens estáticas). Depois, selecionou uma dessas "fotos" e fez uma busca reversa no Google Lens. Assim, chegou ao registro original .

O vídeo foi compartilhado no antigo canal do YouTube da Secretaria de Território e Habitação do Distrito Federal, em 7 de março de 2012. Após reestruturações em 2019, a pasta passou a se chamar Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Urbano e Habitação (Seduh).

Nos primeiros iniciais e finais, a gravação exibe estas legendas, indicando a data e origem do material:

"Lídervideo apresenta: Brasília, a capital do futuro";

"Presidente Juscelino Kubitscheck de Oliveira: Depoimento para a História";

"TV TUPI - Rio de Janeiro" , a primeira emissora de televisão brasileira, inaugurada em 1950 e extinguida em 1980, durante a ditadura militar.

O Fato ou Fake entrou em contato com a Seduh para obter mais informações sobre o registro. Em resposta, a pasta informou que "não foram localizados, nos registros disponíveis na Secretaria, documentos ou informações adicionais sobre o conteúdo do vídeo que permitam identificar a data em que a entrevista foi gravada ou confirmar se o material foi veiculado à época de sua gravação" .

Trechos do vídeo verdadeiro também aparecem em uma reportagem do g1 , que atribuiu as imagens ao Arquivo Público do Distrito Federal, criado em 1985 para planejar e coordenar o acervo e recolhimento de documentos do Poder Executivo de Brasília.

O Fato ou Fake solicitou ao órgão dados sobre data de gravação e veiculação das imagens. Em resposta, o Centro de Pesquisa enviou o arquivo completo, mas afirmou que não havia nenhuma informação complementar disponível.

articles.title: What Neuroscience Says About Gut Feelings And Decision Making
articles.summary: Business owners make numerous high-stakes decisions every day. When they can integrate analytical reasoning and intuition, they can improve their business ou...
articles.body:
A snap decision that turns out right gets called instinct. The same snap decision gone wrong gets called recklessness. Neuroscience has spent three decades mapping what actually happens in the body before we say yes or no to a decision, and the mechanism is more precise than most leadership advice gives it credit for.

The Body Keeps the Score Before the Mind Does

Neuroscientist Antonio Damasio 's somatic marker hypothesis, developed in the 1990s and tested repeatedly since, states that the body encodes the outcomes of past emotional experiences into physiological signals: a tightening chest, a drop in the stomach, a flush of warmth.

These signals arrive in our consciousness ahead of any deliberate analysis our mind makes. They bias the decision before we have finished reasoning it through. That fast, pre-verbal nudge is what people call a gut feeling.

The evidence for this comes from the Iowa Gambling Task, a card game used in Damasio's lab. Participants choose from decks of cards with different risk profiles. Some participants started generating stress responses to the risky decks before they could consciously explain why those decks were worse. Their bodies flagged the danger before their reasoning caught up.

Other participants, with damage to the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (the region that integrates those bodily signals into decision-making) kept picking from the bad decks, even after they could explain that the decks were bad.

Knowing things and feeling things turned out to be running an separate systems. And the feeling system usually gets there first.

Why Business Owners Feel This More Than Most

Business owners have to take an enormous amount of decisions with incomplete information: who to hire or fire, when to raise money, whether to trust a business partner, when to walk away from a deal .

Each of those decisions leaves a somatic trace.

Over years of running a business, that trace accumulates into a genuinely useful internal database. This is why experienced business owners often sense a bad hire in the first meeting or a bad deal in the first conversation, well before they can articulate the specific red flag.

Yet, business owners ignore their gut feeling when they make high-stakes calls. Not because their gut feelings are wrong. It's because it can't be defended in a boardroom. A feeling that can't be backed by a spreadsheet gets overridden. Only to realize later that the hesitation was an accurate read.

Training the Gut Feelings Instead of Ignoring It

The takeaway from Damasio's research is not to replace rational analysis with instinct and gut feeling. The goal is integration. Before a high-stakes call, it helps to separately name what the analysis says and what your gut says, rather than letting the loudest voice in the room (or in your head) take over completely.

When rational analysis and gut feeling disagree, that disagreement itself is information worth sitting with, rather than resolving immediately in favor of whichever felt more comfortable to admit.

It also helps to build a habit of logging decisions and outcomes. You can easily review which gut feelings paid off and which didn't, so you can calibrate the signal over time. A track record makes clear how reliable your combined decision making process is becoming.

The decisions that quietly define your business results, like who to trust, when to move, when to wait,… rarely come with clean data. Business owners who treat their gut feeling as noise that needs to be overridden, are discarding a signal that neuroscience has spent decades researching. The decision making edge belongs to whoever learns to read both systems at once.

articles.title: Srinagar ghost mall turns into Rs 422cr jewel in auction
articles.summary: India News: SRINAGAR: For years, grass and weeds had more business at Sangarmaal City Centre than shoppers did. Then came the bidders. A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) par.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: For years, grass and weeds had more business at Sangarmaal City Centre than shoppers did. Then came the bidders. A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore after an overnight auction far exceeded what govt had pegged.Bidding opened at 11am on Aug 25 for land in front of and behind Sangarmaal, just behind Kashmir Golf Course and opposite Polo View, a pedestrian-only high-street market lined with cafes and boutique stores. One end of the property touches Chunt Khul, a stream running through Srinagar. Dal Lake is about 1km away. Lal Chowk is within easy reach.That mix of location, scale and commercial potential made this largely underused land a prized piece of real estate.By 1.48am on Aug 26, Sangarmaal became one of J&K’s hottest pieces of public real estate, with officials watching the price race far beyond their Rs 200-crore expectations. The highest bid touched Rs 421.75 crore on a full-lease basis.“My heart was racing as the bid was going up and up. It is an important project for J&K and this bid will open investment in the Union Territory after a long time,” an official said Tuesday.Parmesh Construction Company Ltd, a consortium of Pahalgam Green Hotels, a J&K firm and Bhutani Infra Ltd, emerged as the successful bidder.Sangarmaal City Centre traces its roots to 2015, when then CM Mufti Mohammad Sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture meant to give Srinagar a modern skyline.What emerged was an ambitious complex with landscaped areas, fountains, basement and surface parking, lifts and escalators. Its commercial inventory included 62 shops in the main commercial module, 38 spaces in Craft Bazaar, 11 kiosks, two food courts, a restaurant and 11 office spaces.But the dream never got off the ground. Most shops stayed shut. Buyers who acquired units did not open them. Weeds overran the premises, turning what was meant to be a bustling commercial hub into a near-deserted property.Now, a fresh lease could mean a fresh start. The front and rear portions have been offered for development on a full-lease basis, with a multiplex and other commercial facilities proposed.The Sangarmaal auction also set the stage for another high-stakes property bid. At Batamaloo, about 6km away, roughly 70 kanals (8.75 acre) of bus-stand land has remained largely underused and vulnerable to encroachment. Srinagar Development Authority (SDA) is seeking to redevelop it for better use.Bidding opened at Rs 95 crore on Aug 27 and climbed to Rs 305 crore by evening, with Construction Engineers, another J&K consortium, emerging as highest bidder. Batamaloo is also being offered on a full-lease basis, with plans for shopping, office spaces and housing.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Hunter Biden says Kamala Harris is getting 'bad political advice,' refuses to explain loyalty criticism
articles.summary: Hunter Biden said Kamala Harris is getting bad political advice but refuses to fully explain why he thinks she's not a very good politician.
articles.body: Former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, said Sunday that former Vice President Kamala Harris was getting bad political advice after he refused to explain why he thinks she wasn't a good politician. Zeteo founder and former MSNBC host Mehdi Hasan pressed Biden on why he said that Harris was "not a very good politician" despite her repeatedly refusing to break from Joe Biden on key issues while campaigning in 2024. "Here's what I'd also like to say about the vice president. I think that the vice president served the country incredibly well and that she has a deep, rich future in politics. Whether she wants to run for president again, she'll be one of the, if not, the frontrunner," he said. Hasan pressed, "But she's not a very good politician?" HUNTER BIDEN REVEALS HE NEVER WANTED JOE BIDEN TO RUN FOR RE-ELECTION, BUT REFUSED TO TELL HIM TO STOP "No, and I think that the way that she's going about it right now is, at least from my perspective …," Biden began, as Hasan pressed him to elaborate. Biden said, "I think that this administration, unlike you, I don't think that she should have ever been any daylight between, she can make daylight between herself and my dad, but not in terms of what they were able to accomplish over that four-year period. I think that there might be daylight as issues related to Gaza and as it relates to Israel that of course, she needs to be able to stake her own ground on that." The Zeteo founder noted that Harris didn't really break from Biden on Gaza or Israel. Biden insisted Harris' refusal to break with his father on the issue didn't have anything to do with his father. "He didn't pressure her? No daylight, kid?" Hasan asked. A post-2024 election book by reporters Jonathan Allen and Amie Parnes said Joe Biden had told Harris repeatedly that there could be "no daylight" between them and reported that he told her, "No daylight, kid," during a call ahead of her debate with Donald Trump. KAMALA HARRIS LEAVES BIDEN OFF LIST OF TOP THREE 'MOST EFFECTIVE' PRESIDENTS The former president denied doing this during an interview on "The View." "Nothing to do with loyalty to my dad, from my perspective. But here's the thing, is this, is that, you know what? She's a free agent now. I'm Hunter Biden," he said. "I get to think whatever the hell that I want to think about anybody." Hasan pressed him again, questioning, "I'm asking why do you think she's not a very good politician?" "That's between me and her," Hunter Biden told Hasan. Hasan responded and said, "You can't just dangle that out." HUNTER BIDEN REVEALS HE'S 'DEFINITELY NOT RUNNING' FOR OFFICE DESPITE MEDIA TOUR "You know why I can? Because I ain't running for anything, Mehdi, I can say whatever the f--- I want," Biden shot back. Hunter Biden said he did not agree with the perspective that Harris was loyal to his father throughout her campaign. "I think that she was loyal to my father, and I don't think she was loyal to a fault, however. There are certain things she was not loyal on. I think right now her recent appearances that I've seen and what she's trying to distance herself from my dad, the things that she wrote in her book, that we're not loyal in any way. And, so, there is not like this 100%," he said. Later in the interview, during a discussion about a possible 2028 ticket, Biden said he would love for Harris to be president of the United States. "I would love for her to be president of the United States. I think she would make a great president of the United States. I just think that, right now, she's getting bad political advice. That's it," he said. Harris' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Author and psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital, "Harris’s problem was psychological as much as political: Voters wanted change, and she couldn’t bring herself to say what she would change. That was the trap. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "She was so careful about showing loyalty to Biden that she never established a strong identity of her own. When she was asked what she would have done differently, she struggled to give voters a clear answer. "Voters cast their vote on leadership, confidence and authenticity. If the country is unhappy with the person in charge, you can’t run as the change candidate while essentially saying, 'I wouldn’t have changed much.'"

articles.title: Built in 1881 and closed in 2004 over structural problems, a Smithsonian building restored for $55 million has finally been chosen for a permanent new life
articles.summary: US News: The Smithsonian Institution Board of Regents has officially chosen the historic Arts and Industries Building on the National Mall as the permanent hom.
articles.body: The Smithsonian Institution Board of Regents has officially chosen the historic Arts and Industries Building on the National Mall as the permanent home of the National Museum of the American Latino. The decision ends a long debate over the museum’s location and removes the need for Congress to approve a new site because the Smithsonian already owns the building. In an official statement issued on 31 August, the board said converting the existing building completes a multi-year site review authorised by Congress in December 2020. First opened in 1881 as the United States National Museum, the Arts and Industries Building is the second-oldest building in the Smithsonian complex. Structural problems forced it to close completely in 2004, followed by years of deterioration. A $55 million restoration later strengthened the roof and exterior, allowing temporary exhibitions and special events to return.According to The Washington Post, choosing an existing building means the Smithsonian can avoid a long congressional debate over unused land on the National Mall. Other sites considered included open areas near the Capitol reflecting pool and undeveloped land controlled by the National Park Service. Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chair Adriano Espaillat welcomed the decision after the board's vote. “Today the Smithsonian Board of Regents chose to house the National Museum of the American Latino in a prominent location on the National Mall. The Arts and Industries Building -- a true jewel -- will shine like never before as the new, permanent home for this great American project,” said CHC Chair Espaillat in a public statement. “It has been a personal privilege to be part of turning this idea into a reality. This is a great victory for the Latino community, which until now has lacked a ship to take our story to port.”Overcoming political resistance and site hurdlesThe decision to reuse an existing building comes after years of political debate over the museum. Reports from Reuters and The New York Times said the project faced opposition from congressional Republicans, while budget proposals from the Trump administration sought to remove dedicated construction funding and instead support exhibits spread across different Smithsonian museums. Because the Smithsonian already owns the Arts and Industries Building, the decision removes the need for new federal legislation to approve the site. The Smithsonian said the choice moves the project directly into the development process set out by Congress when it authorised the museum in 2020. The National Museum of the American Latino opened its first physical preview space, the Molina Family Latino Gallery, inside the National Museum of American History in 2022. The gallery was created to host temporary exhibitions for up to 10 years while plans for a permanent museum were developed. Jorge Zamanillo, director of the National Museum of the American Latino, has previously said creating a dedicated museum building would take many years. “It will take 10 to 12 years to open a museum building, but the gallery gives the public a preview of the museum's potential,” said Jorge Zamanillo during the opening of the Molina Family Latino Gallery.Architectural heritage and future conversion costsArchitects Adolf Cluss and Paul Schulze designed the Arts and Industries Building, which was built to display exhibits from the 1876 Philadelphia Centennial Exposition. Made with colourful brick and geometric tilework, the red-brick landmark stands next to the original Smithsonian Institution Building, known as the Castle. Despite its historic importance, converting the 19th-century building into a modern museum will require major engineering work and investment. Early estimates reported by Reuters suggest that upgrading the interior, adding climate control and expanding exhibition areas could cost about $1 billion. The Smithsonian will need major private donations as well as federal funding to pay for the interior reconstruction. The earlier $55 million restoration protected the building’s outer structure from serious damage, but the inside is still largely an open, high-ceilinged space that needs a complete modernisation. The selection of the Arts and Industries Building ends the debate over the museum’s location and gives Latino history and culture a permanent place on the National Mall. The Smithsonian is expected to provide more details on architectural plans and fundraising for the interior work during upcoming board briefings.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A 16th-century English longhouse hid serious structural problems behind its walls; the builder restoring it has now turned the centuries-old property into his own family home
articles.summary: US News: Cadman Construction was already undertaking one of its most challenging heritage projects: restoring a Grade II-listed 16th-century longhouse in Suffo.
articles.body: Cadman Construction was already undertaking one of its most challenging heritage projects: restoring a Grade II-listed 16th-century longhouse in Suffolk. But for Stuart Cadman, Managing Director of Cadman Construction the challenge had an additional dimension: the centuries-old property was finally to be his family home. The restoration included repairing much of the original oak frame, but also creating contemporary spaces that met the needs of modern family living. At all stages there was a balancing act between preserving historic fabric and meeting current construction standards, conservation requirements and the practical realities of restoring a building more than 400 years old, states an interview with Cadman published by the Heritage and Traditional Building website. Some of the biggest challenges didn’t emerge until we were actually working on it, mentioned Cadman in the interview. It was mentioned that at the south end of the house, the original oak frame was found to be a mix of oak and softwood. Much of the softwood had rotted beyond the point where it could be safely supported. The south chimney was also identified as a hybrid construction with limited historic significance. According to the interview, the findings meant the project required a new planning application and Listed Building Consent to enable demolition and rebuilding of much of the southern section. Restoration was delayed by approximately six months due to approval processes, the report adds.Piece by piece, holding up a 400-year-old buildingThe restoration team chose a more cautious approach rather than trying to support the whole building at once. The first floor perimeter beam was supported in six-metre lengths by a propping system designed by a structural engineer. Then, each section could be carefully checked before repairs were made. The team followed the same process throughout the rest of the building after successfully completing the first part. The technique reduced risk and left the historic oak frame largely intact while its condition was assessed. For a centuries-old structure, it was imperative to proceed with caution. The project showed that restoring heritage requires as much patience as technical expertise.Where 16th-century character meets modern lifeThe new extensions were built to modern building standards but designed to be visually compatible with the original longhouse. The old and the new were intentionally kept different. Modern windows and construction details help distinguish the additions from the historic structure, but the design as a whole allows the additions to sit comfortably next to the historic structure. No less significant were the traditional materials. For the existing building, the choice fell on William Blyth clay pantiles and locally sourced lime render. Lime render also has a functional role in historic construction. Older buildings breathe and traditional materials allow moisture to regulate itself, rather than being trapped inside the building.Collaboration and craftsmanshipThe restoration needed close cooperation between contractors, conservation specialists, structural engineers and local authorities. This type of collaboration is especially important for listed buildings, where even minor changes can often require a long process of assessment and approval. The experience also highlighted the need for patience when working with historic properties. Specialist craftsmanship remained central to the project, supported by modern techniques to maintain the character of the original structure.Saving the past for another 400 yearsFor Cadman and his family, finishing the restoration is about more than moving into a beautifully renovated home. It means helping to secure the future of a building which has stood for more than four centuries. The original structure and chimneys might date from craftsmen working during the reign of Henry VIII, placing the property within a remarkable stretch of English history. The completed house is a marriage of two very different time periods. The historic fabric is visible and respected, while contemporary additions offer the comfort and performance expected of a modern family property. The project has also boosted Cadman Construction’s confidence in heritage work, giving the company greater insight into the risks, processes and practical challenges involved in listed-building restoration. For this centuries-old Suffolk longhouse the goal was never to restore what had been lost. To keep the story of the building alive, to write another chapter in it that would last for centuries.Images Courtesy: Heritage and Traditional BuildingCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Spanish government approves €309 million aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis
articles.summary: Spain's Economy Minister said the aid package represents a 'shock response' designed to meet the demands of social organisations and the city government.
articles.body:
The migrant crisis in Ceuta continues to dominate Spain's political agenda.

The Council of Ministers on Tuesday approved an extraordinary funding package worth €309 million for the autonomous city, aimed at safeguarding jobs, supporting businesses, strengthening security and ensuring public services.

Government spokesperson Elma Saiz presented the measures alongside First Vice-President Carlos Cuerpo and Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres. The announcement came on the eve of a demonstration in the city that has exposed divisions in the PSOE and prompted Podemos to call a separate anti-racism rally.

The package, Cuerpo explained, amounts to around 16% of the city's GDP over the four remaining months of 2026.

The money is divided into four areas: €21 million for healthcare, education, justice and water treatment; more than €90 million for defence and the national security forces; €118 million for humanitarian care of unaccompanied migrant minors; and €80 million in direct support for businesses, incentives for trade and tax cuts.

Cuerpo, who also serves as Economy Minister, said the aid package represents a "shock response" designed to meet the demands of social organisations and the city government.

He said that the main aim of the decree was "to give confidence" to both companies and workers.

Cuerpo also stressed that, before the migration crisis, Ceuta was going through a "period of economic dynamism" that had helped to correct some of the "structural deficits" the city had struggled with for decades.

Direct aid for businesses and the self-employed

Of the €80 million allocated for businesses, €36.6 million is earmarked for direct support: €5,000 per self-employed worker and between €10,000 and €150,000 per company, depending on turnover.

Applications can be submitted from Monday 14 via the Tax Agency website, with the first payments aiming to arrive in early October.

The government has estimated that the measure will benefit 2,600 self-employed workers and 1,400 companies. This is supplemented by €14 million in consumer and tourism vouchers, €1 million for the Plan Ceuta Exporta, and another €1 million to promote the city as an international tourist destination.

The package also includes permanent measures: Corporation Tax relief rises from 50% to 60% for companies in Ceuta and Melilla that maintain their activity and jobs, alongside improvements to personal income tax (IRPF) for the self-employed, totalling €12 million.

Employers' Social Security contributions are to be subsidised from 50% to 75% for permanent contracts linked to training, at a cost of €12.2 million over four months.

The government will also set up an ICO-backed loan guarantee scheme worth up to €50 million, introduce exemptions for companies that make use of the job retention scheme (ERTE) and provide an extraordinary benefit for self-employed workers who are forced to stop working.

The president of the Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, warned of the seriousness of the situation a month ago, when the Government approved a first package of €168 million euros for the territory.

Vivas reiterated this in a new text, published by PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, in which he denounced an "attack on its territorial integrity" and described a city "overwhelmed and on the brink of collapse."

Vivas calls for Spanish unity on Ceuta Day

Vivas has also addressed Spaniards across the country in a message marking Ceuta Day, which is celebrated on 2 September, amid the fallout from the migrant crisis.

In his letter, Vivas called for national unity and solidarity and thanked people for the support shown to Ceuta in recent weeks.

"Ceuta has lived through its toughest month this August," he added in the text, in which he described recent events as "an unprecedented outrage" against the territory.

But whatever happens, he insisted that the city would "never" be abandoned.

Vivas also acknowledged that this year's 2 September celebrations would be different from those of previous years.

However, in his view, the situation the city is facing has made this day "particularly significant" and has presented an opportunity to strengthen ties and unity among Spaniards.

The president also referred to the rallies scheduled for 8 pm in municipalities across Spain following a call by the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces (FEMP).

He stressed that these demonstrations were not intended to serve partisan interests and are "not marked by political colours or ideologies."

Their purpose, he said, was to send a message of unity and support to Ceuta.

Another of the key messages in the letter is that the defence of Ceuta goes far beyond the territory itself.

"The cause is not exclusively Ceuta's; it is the cause of all Spain," he said, linking the defence of the city to protecting territorial integrity and democratic values.

"We have never stopped feeling you at our side," Vivas continued, while also expressing gratitude for the support shown towards the city during "its most difficult moment."

He added that such displays had been "a source of encouragement and hope" and had helped send Ceutans a clear message: "We are not alone".

articles.title: Jynxzi announces 100-player Fortnite tournament: Who will join Ludwig, Valkyrae and Tyler1 in 50-duo showdown?
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Gaming streamer Jynxzi is bringing 100 creators together for a Fortnite tournament featuring 50 duos. The event is scheduled for September 20, 2026, a.
articles.body: Gaming streamer Jynxzi is bringing 100 creators together for a Fortnite tournament featuring 50 duos. The event is scheduled for September 20, 2026, at 4 PM ET, with viewers in the UK able to watch from 9 PM BST. Jynxzi has already revealed a large part of the lineup, with creators including Ludwig, Valkyrae, Tyler1, SypherPK, Stable Ronaldo, Sketch and Emiru among those confirmed. He also explained how he plans to keep the competition balanced, saying some experienced Fortnite players will have to use controllers during the event.Jynxzi confirms 38 streamers for 100-player Fortnite tournamentJynxzi announced the tournament on X and asked streamers to find a duo and sign up for the event.He wrote:“Need 100 Streamers for Fortnite Tourney September 20th 4PM ET Tag your duo.”During a recent stream, Jynxzi revealed the creators who had already confirmed their spots. The list includes a mix of gaming creators, streamers and personalities from different parts of the online community.The confirmed participants are Bradley Martyn, CourageJD, Vikkstar, Ludwig, SypherPK, Deji, FaZe Adapt, FaZe Rug, Agent, MrArthur, Flight, Russell, AngryGinge, LosPollos, Valkyrae, Zoil, RoyalPenguin, Tbvnks, Tyler1, ohnePixel, ItzTimmy, Emiru, Stable Ronaldo, Dantes, Rynenzo, Martin, JankyRondo, Yusuf, Mingo, Joe Bart, Arky, Jason, Lacy, Sketch, Togi, Hamza, VanillaMace and KatieB.With 100 players expected to take part, the tournament will have plenty of familiar faces from the streaming world. The remaining spots are expected to be filled as more creators choose their duos.The event is set to begin at 4 PM ET/3 PM CT/1 PM PT/9 PM BST on September 20.Jynxzi says top Fortnite players will use controllersThe presence of experienced Fortnite players raised a different question. Some viewers wondered whether players such as Stable Ronaldo and SypherPK would have too much of an advantage over creators who do not regularly play Fortnite.Jynxzi said he plans to reduce that gap by putting several strong players on controllers.He specifically mentioned Ronaldo, Lacy, SypherPK and CourageJD as players who would face the restriction.Jynxzi said:“Ron is winning? We’re hard-nerfing Ron. Ron and Lacey.”He then explained that Ronaldo would use a controller and could be paired with Flight or LosPollos. Jynxzi also said Lacy would have a controller teammate and confirmed that SypherPK and CourageJD would also be required to use controllers.He added:“If you’re one of those, like, Fortnite YouTubers or Fortnite streamers, we have to put you on a controller because there are people in here literally asking me how to build.”The controller rule is designed to make the matches less one-sided when experienced Fortnite players compete alongside creators who may not have the same level of experience with the game.Jynxzi has not yet revealed all 50 duos or provided a full tournament format. More details could be announced as the September 20 event gets closer.For now, the confirmed lineup already includes some of the biggest names in streaming, giving the 100-player Fortnite tournament a mix of competitive players and creators who are better known for other types of content.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tribunal alters gay ex-IAF man 'dismissal' to 'routine discharge'
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to being gay, into a routine discharge.The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces.The non-commissioned IAF officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry. The inquiry concluded he had breached discipline and risked national security by entering into a relationship with a foreigner. The court of inquiry also found him guilty of travelling abroad (Thailand and Sri Lanka) without permission. He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 91-year-old Tennessee man Dale Sanders, known as ‘Grey Beard’, completes 2,193-mile Appalachian Trail after 71 falls, including 6 hard falls, reclaims record as oldest hiker
articles.summary: US News: Dale Sanders has reclaimed his record as the oldest person to complete the Appalachian Trail after hiking 2,193 miles (3,530 kilometres) across the ea.
articles.body: Dale Sanders has reclaimed his record as the oldest person to complete the Appalachian Trail after hiking 2,193 miles (3,530 kilometres) across the eastern United States at the age of 91.The Tennessee man, whose trail name is “Grey Beard”, counted 71 falls during his latest attempt, including six he described as particularly hard. One resulted in a brief hospitalisation, while another happened just 200 yards from the finish, as reported by AP.Despite the setbacks, Sanders refused to let the falls permanently derail his journey along the iconic trail, which stretches from Springer Mountain in Georgia to Mount Katahdin in Maine.He completed the hike on Monday at the summit of Maine’s highest peak. At the trail's endpoint, Sanders paused to pray at the sign marking the summit and thanked God, his support team and everyone who had helped him complete the challenge.Dale Sanders first set the record at 82Sanders first became the oldest person to complete the Appalachian Trail in 2017, when he was 82. Four years later, 83-year-old M.J. Eberhart, known on the trail as “Nimblewill Nomad”, surpassed his record.Sanders subsequently announced plans to reclaim the title, but his second attempt proved considerably more demanding than his first.Although he had trained for six months before returning to the trail, Sanders admitted that he did not feel he was in his best physical condition.He said his age was ultimately a reminder of just how unusual his achievement was, noting that at 91 he was “blazing new ground” by taking on such long-distance hikes.Six serious falls and a hospital scareThe physical challenges became particularly intense during Sanders’ journey.In June, while descending Killington Mountain in Vermont, he fell forward in a boulder field, scraping his legs, arms and hands. Thankfully, he avoided any broken bones and continued hiking despite being badly bruised and bloodied.Several weeks later, his left arm became numb and he was taken to a hospital in Maine. Doctors initially feared that he had suffered a stroke, but the problem was ultimately diagnosed as a pinched nerve.Although Sanders was cleared to return to the trail, the experience made him consider abandoning the attempt.He briefly returned to his home in Tennessee in early August to support his wife following the death of her mother. His wife encouraged him to continue, and Sanders eventually resumed his journey.His mission became bigger than reclaiming the recordAs Sanders travelled through different sections of the Appalachian Trail, he discovered that his journey had begun to mean more than simply reclaiming his title.Some of his favourite stretches were in Pennsylvania, where he enjoyed well-maintained trails and support from so-called “trail angels” who brought him food and drinks.Sanders also attracted a growing following online, something that surprised him. Thousands of people began tracking his progress and sharing messages of encouragement.While reclaiming the record remained an important goal, Sanders said inspiring other people had gradually become more significant.His journey also left an impression on fellow hikers. Meredith Ewenson, who encountered Sanders while leading a group hike in New Hampshire, said seeing him tackle the trail at 91 was an experience she would remember for years.She recalled being stunned by his mobility and fitness, particularly given his age.Sanders has completed several extraordinary challengesSanders was born in Kentucky in 1935, two years before the Appalachian Trail was completed. He was bullied as a child because of his small stature but gained confidence through individual sports including acrobatics and swimming.He later served in the US Navy and spent a long career working in parks and recreation before retiring in 2002.The Appalachian Trail is far from his only endurance achievement. Sanders has also set several age-related records, including becoming the oldest person to paddle the entire length of the Mississippi River. He completed the 87-day journey after beginning it on his 87th birthday.During his latest Appalachian Trail adventure, Sanders continued to tackle fallen trees, steep sections and difficult scrambles despite the physical toll.On one 12-mile (19-kilometre) day, he became so tired that he lay down on the trail and announced that he needed a “power nap”. He briefly fell asleep before getting back up just two minutes later and continuing his hike.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
